note: Pose measurements taken off the target reference photo (a loaded Olympic bar shot from its own midline). These are what the camera constants in src/components/weight/three/scale.ts are derived from. Pixel figures come from the 649x325 source; ratios are what actually carry over.
method: Threshold the object against the white backdrop, take the per-column vertical extent, then read the innermost plate's face ellipse off the inner silhouette. The ellipse is sampled where sqrt(1 - ((y-cy)/b)^2) = 0.5, i.e. at y = cy +/- 0.866b, because the apex is both noisy and biased.

deviations.why: The reference bar is stylised and short — its collar sits 0.48 of the half length out, where a real Olympic bar's sits at 0.6. Real 220cm / 45cm proportions were kept so that picking a 35 or a 25 reads as a genuinely smaller plate.
0.19 is thicker than any real bumper and would push a six-plate stack off the end of the sleeve. 0.16 is the most the sleeve takes while still leaving the tip visible.
Longer than a real 41cm sleeve, but required: at this view angle the outermost plate's near rim projects almost as far out as the tip, so a real-length sleeve leaves a loaded bar with no visible tip.
